F292's BEGIN IMMEDIATE mitigation is measured and REFUTED AS A FIX (iteration 2): it reproduced on the mitigated tree at f51ec21, 1 red in 17 runs against 11 in 41 without. The finding is five weeks old, it is the single largest source of CI red on this project, and the measurement bought a genuinely new narrowing -- the holder is present BEFORE the schema reset begins, which is strictly narrower than anything the entry has carried. The merge gate has opened once ever, and iteration 4 completed the diagnosis. Three distinct timing failures are now on record: checking at a firing's START finds an in-flight run (iteration 2); checking at the END finds the run still in flight if the firing is shorter than the build (iteration 3); and at iteration 4 condition 3 HELD FOR THE FIRST TIME -- CI concluded success for HEAD 35cdd38 -- while condition 2 failed, because a firing that has done its work has a dirty tree by definition and one that has committed has moved HEAD to a sha CI has not built. The gate as written can only pass in a gap no firing occupies. The fix is to gate on the newest sha on the branch with a CONCLUDED green run rather than on HEAD. That is a day-window.md step 1 edit, so the operator's. Everything else held at iteration 4: master is 0 commits ahead of the branch, no HOLD MERGE.

F306's R1 measurement raises a question about the finding ledger's suggestions, not just this finding. Two of the three shapes F306 proposed for its own fix are now measured wrong -- kind-scoping is unimplementable against a free-form field, and the guard fallback it named would have refused every flow-staffed review. Both read as plausible and neither had been run. Nothing is broken by this (a round caught both, which is what rounds are for), but if the ledger's shape-of-a-fix lists are being read as a head start by later windows, they are worth a pass that labels them as unverified sketches.

A method question raised by R2 on F306, not a one-off. R1 measured 'blast radius' over 15 test files chosen by fixture style (the suites seeding evidence through review_evidence.py, plus the review/guard/staffing suites), got 210 green, and wrote 'zero blast radius'. The whole Hub suite is 4131 tests and found one failure -- in the file whose fixture is literally the defect being fixed. Worth deciding whether 'blast radius' in a proposal should mean the whole suite by default. The cost is real: the whole suite takes 26 minutes on this machine, affordable inside a 5-minute-firing loop only when started in the background at the top of a firing. Not changed unilaterally, because the rounds are already expensive and this makes one of them longer.

F316 (A) was filed by a spec-loop round rather than by a drive, and its repair is folded into F306's change (task 2.4) rather than given its own.
